name: Sickle Cell S-Lepore Disease

criteria.description: Presence of hemoglobin S and hemoglobin Lepore detected by hemoglobin electrophoresis or HPLC
Clinical manifestations consistent with sickle cell disease including vaso-occlusive crises and hemolytic anemia
Molecular confirmation of HBB gene mutations encoding hemoglobin S and Lepore fusion variant
Exclusion of other hemoglobinopathies by comprehensive hemoglobin analysis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Detection of hemoglobin S and Lepore variant by electrophoresis or genetic testing plus clinical features consistent with sickle cell disease
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires integration of laboratory, genetic, and clinical findings due to rarity and overlap with other hemoglobinopathies.

pathognomonic.notes: Recurrent episodes of severe pain due to microvascular occlusion
Persistent anemia with reticulocytosis and elevated LDH
searchTerms: long-term destruction of red blood cells
chronic anemia from red cell breakdown

common.notes: Yellow discoloration of skin and sclera
searchTerms: yellow skin from red blood cell breakdown

common.notes: Painful swelling of hands and feet in young children
searchTerms: painful swelling of hands and feet

common.notes: Growth retardation secondary to chronic disease
Due to functional asplenia and immune dysfunction

occasional.notes: Pulmonary infiltrates with chest pain and hypoxia
searchTerms: acute lung syndrome with chest pain
sudden chest pain and breathing trouble

occasional.notes: Chronic non-healing ulcers on lower extremities
Due to chronic hemolysis and bilirubin overload
Sudden enlargement of spleen with acute anemia

searchTerms: stroke or brain blood vessel accident

rare.notes: Bone infarction leading to joint destruction
searchTerms: loss of blood supply to femoral head

rare.notes: Elevated pulmonary arterial pressure secondary to chronic hemolysis
Vascular changes in retina due to sickling

laboratory: Hemoglobin electrophoresis showing Hb S and Hb Lepore bands
imaging: MRI brain showing ischemic lesions in stroke
X-ray or MRI showing avascular necrosis of femoral head
Chest X-ray showing acute chest syndrome infiltrates
other: Functional asplenia demonstrated by absence of splenic uptake on radionuclide scan
Peripheral blood smear showing sickled erythrocytes and target cells

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of homozygous Hb S without Lepore fusion
Genetic testing negative for Lepore variant
Presence of Hb Lepore without Hb S

redFlags: Sudden onset of severe bone pain indicating vaso-occlusive crisis
Acute neurological deficits suggestive of stroke
Rapidly enlarging painful spleen indicating splenic sequestration
references: Steinberg MH. Management of sickle cell disease. N Engl J Med. 1999;340(13):1021-30.
